# dsh-session-workspace-organizer
> A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: move a workspace folder to a new location, give every new session
its own output folder, and restart the desktop app from the header.
English | 简体中文
DSH binds each session to a workspace directory, and every session of that workspace shares it — so
scripts, logs, downloads and screenshots from unrelated conversations pile up in the same place. Thi
s plugin adds four things on top of that model, without patching DSH itself:
1. **Relocate a workspace** — move the folder to another path or disk and take its sessions with it.
Every session log's header `cwd` is rewritten to the new path, so sessions keep working and stay li

sted under the new workspace.
2. **One output folder per session** — each new or resumed session get
s `<workspace>/sessions/<YYYY-MM-DD>_<title>/`, the model is told (through a session-scoped system p
rompt) to write its artifacts there, and a `write` that would create a file at the workspace root as

ks for confirmation first.
3. **Session management** — move idle sessions to another workspace, or d

elete them (with a dry-run preview), optionally together with the files they created.
4. **Header re
start** — a restart button that ends and relaunches the whole DSH process, with a confirmation dialo
g, a busy-work guard and a progress layer instead of a frozen page.
Tested with DSH Desktop `0.2.1-rc.2` on Windows. Host code uses Node built-ins only; the client is a
hand-written CommonJS bundle, so there is no build step.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
On the **Desktop app**, use the Plugins page: remove the old entry, then install `dsh-session-worksp
ace-organizer` or `github:dream-fish69/dsh-session-workspace-organizer` from the install field. Rest
art DSH after installing or upgrading — the Host half is only loaded at startup.
Uninstall:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Removing the plugin leaves the `sessions/` folders and their files alone.
## Where the UI lives
**Settings → Workspaces** (the section title follows the DSH language: `工作区` in Chinese). Three thin
orkspaces** (the section title follows the DSH language: `工作区` in Chinese). Three things live there:
### Move workspace
Pick a registered workspace, choose a target parent folder and type the new folder name.
The plugin then performs a **strict relocation**:
- the whole directory — `sessions/` included — is moved to the new path, and the **old path is delet

ed**; no junction or symlink is left behind;
- each session log whose header `cwd` equals the old pa
th is rewritten: the first zstd frame carries the header, only its `cwd` is replaced, and every late
r frame is kept byte-identical; the log directory is then moved from `--<old cwd>--` to `--<new cwd>

--`;
- the workspace is re-registered from the new path and sessions are attached to it; sessions th
is running process cannot attach yet are recorded in `pending-attach.json` and attached automaticall

y after a DSH restart;
- a cross-disk move copies first and verifies file by file, keeps the source

until the copy is verified, and rolls back on failure;
- if the old directory is locked (Windows `EB
USY`/`EPERM`/`EACCES` — e.g. DSH still holds a handle), the plugin falls back to a copy migration: c
opy and verify, rewrite the copied logs, switch the registry, then delete the old directory if it ca
n and report the exact reason when it cannot.
**Hard requirement:** the workspace being moved must have no running session, because session logs a
re append-only and a live write handle cannot be rewritten safely. Open a conversation in **another*
* workspace and trigger the move from there. If sessions are still running, a dialog lists them (tit
le + id) and offers to cancel their turns, wait for them to settle, and continue with the copy path
— unless the session you are typing in is itself in the target workspace, which always has to be mov
on you are typing in is itself in the target workspace, which always has to be moved from elsewhere.
If the old path was DSH's launch directory, the plugin also switches the process working directory a
nd the sandbox fallback root, but desktop shortcuts or launcher configuration still have to be updat
box fallback root, but desktop shortcuts or launcher configuration still have to be updated by hand.
## Compatibility and limitations

- DSH `0.2.x` (Web and Desktop profiles that include `dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app`).
- Busy-handle hand

ling keys off Windows error codes; on other platforms the copy fallback is simply the normal path.
-
Movement and deletion run as commands recorded in an open conversation, so a session must be open;

that session must not belong to the workspace being moved.
- The sidebar's workspace "…" menu has no
extension slot in DSH, which is why the entry point lives in Settings.
## How it works
| Layer | File | Responsibility |
| Host | `index.js` | Registers the `workspace-relocate-check` / `workspace-relocate-strict` / `work
space-organize` / `session-relocate-plan` / `session-relocate` / `session-relocate-batch` / `session
-delete-preview` / `session-delete` / `session-delete-batch` commands; `agent/created` builds the se
ssion folder and the scoped prompt; `session/event` renames it on title change; `tools/pre-execute`

guards root writes; serves the restart route |
| Host | `lib/fs-ops.js` | Directory move (same-disk

rename, cross-disk copy + verify + rollback), name sanitizing, loose-file scan |
| Host | `lib/sessi
on-logs.js` | zstd first-frame header parsing, `cwd`-only rewrite, later frames untouched, log-direc

tory re-homing |
| Host | `lib/restart.js` | Full-process restart: shell-first shutdown (so no nativ

e error dialog), detached relaunch helper, liveness check, bounded restart logs |
| Client | `client
.js` | `settings.section` page with the move / organize / sessions dialogs, the header restart butto
n and its confirmation/progress layers, bilingual copy from `locale/*.json` |
